NOTE ON USAGE :
When indicating possession, the most commonly used verb in British English is have got (in present tense forms) , have got:
`Have you got any pets?' `Yes, I've got three rabbits and a tortoise.' ?, .

In US English (and commonly in tenses other than the present in British English) have is used , have, have, :
I have an apartment in downtown Manhattan. .
*  I haven't got a car now but I'll have one next week. , .

Have when used in the present tense in British English is more formal than have got *have, have got:
I have no objection to your proposal. .

In British English have got, indicating possession, behaves like an auxiliary verb and a pp , have got, :
`Have you got a computer?' `Yes, I have.' ?.

In US English questions and negatives are formed with do , do:
`Do you have a computer?' `Yes I do.' ?.

This construction is common in British English in tenses other than the present :
I didn't have any money so I couldn't get a newspaper. , .

It is also increasingly found in the present tense. .

senses.definition: 用法见have2,3. (Brit also have got) (not used in the continuous tenses 不用于进行时态).
possess or own (sth) 有, 据有（某物）: He has a house in London and a cottage near the sea. 他在伦敦有一所房子, 在海边还有一个小屋.

examples.text: Do you have any pets?
They've got two cars.
How many glasses have we got?
Do you have/Have you got a 50p piece?
examples.translation: 你有没有一枚50便士的硬币?

senses.definition: possess or display (a mental quality or physical feature) 有, 具有（某种精神素质或生理特点）: You must have a lot of courage. 你可真有胆量.

examples.text: She has a good memory.
Giraffes have long necks.
The house has (ie contains) three bedrooms.
You've got a cut on your chin.
have a tooth loose/missing

senses.definition: (be able to) make use of or exercise (sth) （有能力）利用或运用（某事物）: She has no real power. 她没有实权.

examples.text: I don't have the authority to send them home.

examples.translation: 我不再担负过去那样多的责任了.

examples.text: Have you got time to phone him?
examples.translation: 你有时间给他打电话吗?

senses.definition: experience or feel (sth); keep in the mind (used esp with the ns shown) 体验或感到（某事物）; 心存, 心怀（尤与下列名词连用）: I have no doubt (ie I am sure) that you are right. 我肯定你说得对.

examples.translation: 我们在夏天往往请母亲来住上一个月.

examples.translation: 他走出法庭时耷拉着脑袋.

senses.definition: be aware of (sth) as a duty or necessity 对（某事物）觉得有责任或有必要: He has a lot of homework (to do) tonight. 他今晚有许多家庭作业（要做）.

examples.text: She's got a family to feed.
